chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Aban, from al-Fudayl, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no problem if the man were to apply Al-Khalouq, but he should not sleep overnight having applied Al-Khalouq.

key_terms.مُتَخَلِّقاً: having applied Al-Khalouq (state of being scented)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sleep with perfume on according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this ruling from Imam al-Baqir (AS), reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the early Shia community regarding personal hygiene and social etiquette. The prohibition against sleeping with *Al-Khalouq* on is interpreted by scholars as a measure to preserve the scent for morning prayers or to prevent the strong odor from disturbing one's spouse, aligning with the broader Islamic emphasis on cleanliness (*Taharah*) and consideration for others.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Salih Bin Al Sandy, from Ja’far Bin Basheer, from Aban, from Al Fazeyl, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is no problem if the man were to apply Al-Khalouq, but he should not sleep overnight having applied Al-Khalouq’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Salih ibn al-Sindiy from Ja‘far ibn Bashir from Aban from al-Fudayl from a man who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is not harmful to use al-Khuluq, but one must not sleep overnight with it.’”
